text: Create a CKS Kubernetes cluster via the Cloud Console or Terraform
quote: You can create a cluster with the Cloud Console or with Terraform.

text: Deploy multiple Node Pools in one cluster to run different workload types or scale parts independently
quote: You can deploy multiple Node Pools within a single cluster, where each Node Pool contains any number of Nodes. This lets you run different types of workloads on different types of Nodes, or scale different parts of your application independ

text: Autoscale Node Pools with the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler based on GPU/CPU/memory demand
quote: CKS supports scaling Node Pools by using the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler...letting you scale CKS Node Pools in response to workload demands for GPU, CPU, or memory resources.

text: Spot Node Pools give pay-as-you-go bare-metal compute with no long-term commitment
quote: Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.

text: API to create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters
quote: The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.

text: Terraform provider manages CKS clusters, VPC networking, storage, and inference resources as code
quote: The CoreWeave Terraform provider lets you manage CoreWeave infrastructure as code, including CKS clusters, VPC networking, AI Object Storage policies and buckets, and Managed Inference resources.

text: Download a kubeconfig to interact with a cluster via kubectl
quote: Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.

text: API requests are authenticated with a Bearer token access credential
quote: All API requests must include a CoreWeave API access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

text: Official generated clients available for Connect/gRPC/Protobuf across Go, Python, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Swift
quote: Clients are available for the Connect, gRPC, and Protobuf ecosystems across languages including Go, Python, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Swift.

text: S3-compatible storage lets you store training data, checkpoints, and weights with direct access to GPU compute
quote: Store training data, checkpoints, and model weights with efficient S3-compatible access directly to your GPU compute resources.

text: Run Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes so training and inference share the same cluster's compute resources
quote: SUNK enables its users to do the following: Run training and inference workloads on the same cluster by running Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes.

text: View quotas, interpret quota errors, and request capacity increases in the Cloud Console
quote: This page shows you how to view your quotas in the Cloud Console, how to read quota errors when a Node Pool exceeds its quota, and how to request an increase when you need more capacity.

text: Billing insights show billable resource usage and consumption broken down by resource type
quote: Billing insights: View billable resource usage and consumption breakdowns by resource type.

text: CKS runs Kubernetes directly on bare metal nodes with no hypervisor or customer VMs
quote: CKS runs Kubernetes directly on bare metal Nodes, without a hypervisor. Customer clusters don't run Virtual Machines.

text: Inference API gives programmatic control over inference gateways, model deployments, and capacity claims
quote: The CoreWeave Inference API provides programmatic control over inference gateways, model deployments, and capacity claims.

text: Spin up on-demand or spot GPU capacity quickly for burst workloads without long-term commitments
quote: Utilize on-demand GPU instances for additional workloads when you're not looking for long-term capacity commitments. Quickly spin-up burst On-Demand or Spot capacity—with the flexibility of great pricing.

text: Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console compares GPU placement availability across zones before provisioning
quote: Before you create a Spot Node Pool, use Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console to compare placement availability across Zones for your requested instance type and Node count.

text: Inference API can be called over multiple transport protocols depending on client tooling and performance needs
quote: You can call the Inference API over several transport protocols, depending on your client tooling and performance needs

text: CKS is a managed Kubernetes service that runs clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud
quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.
